# Gain-to-pain ratio (`gain_to_pain_ratio`)

*Category: Return summary · Nature: derived · Unit: ratio · Formula id: `gain_to_pain_ratio@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Sum of all returns relative to the sum of losing-period returns.

## 2. Formula

```text
sum(r_t) / |sum(r_t for r_t < 0)|
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

How much net return was earned for each unit of losses suffered along the way.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Schwager's gain-to-pain ratio on per-period returns; a simple, distribution-free complement to volatility-based ratios.

## 7. Assumptions

- Per-period returns are summed (not compounded).

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Very few losing periods exist: the denominator is tiny and the ratio unstable.
- Compared across data frequencies (monthly vs daily values differ).

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations and at least one losing period; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `ratio_standard`: Risk-adjusted ratios: at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.)

## 11. Sources

- Schwager, J. D. (2012). Market Sense and Nonsense. Wiley (Gain-to-Pain ratio).

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Computed on the supplied observation frequency; undefined (not applicable) when no period is negative.
